label: PINCER 6
title: Warfarin without a recent INR check
statement: Patients receiving warfarin for at least three months who have not had a recorded check of their INR within the previous 12 weeks - More specifically, patients with one or more prescriptions for warfarin recorded on computer three to six months prior to data collection and in the three months prior to data collection who have not had a computer-recorded INR within the previous three months.

source.document: Avery AJ, et al. Protocol for the PINCER trial. Trials 2009;10:28; correction Trials 2010;11:23
source.citation: Avery AJ, Rodgers S, Cantrill JA, et al. Protocol for the PINCER trial. Trials 2009;10:28. doi:10.1186/1745-6215-10-28; correction Trials 2010;11:23
source.credit: Avery AJ, Rodgers S, Cantrill JA, et al. Protocol for the PINCER trial. Trials 2009;10:28. doi:10.1186/1745-6215-10-28; correction Trials 2010;11:23

plain_summary: This trial indicator flags ongoing warfarin supply with no INR recorded in the last three calendar months. Queensland community guidance recommends checks every 4 to 6 weeks once the INR is stable and allows up to 8 weeks when it remains very stable.

needs_facts.meets: Whether a recorded INR falls in the three months ending on the last date in the dispensing history. A confirmed gap meets the monitoring criterion. A check recorded in the window rules it out. If the available information cannot establish timing, choose Not known.

options.words: A check was recorded in the three months ending on the last date in the dispensing history
Records confirm there was no check recorded in the three months ending on the last date in the dispensing history

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when warfarin (Group A) is supplied at least once three to six months before the latest date in the record AND at least once in the last three months, AND the record holds no INR in the last three months (the newest INR is older, or there is none). With qualifying supplies, report a finding if the latest dated INR is older than the window or the pharmacist confirms no check was recorded in that window. Cite the supplies and the old test or the confirming answer. A dated check or a pharmacist's confirmation of a recorded check inside the window rules out the finding, whatever the value. If the timing is unknown, including when the only result is undated or no test history is available, report only a possible finding and name "INR" as the missing fact. Use the test date or the period the pharmacist confirmed. The day the answer was entered does not date the test. A recent INR means no finding.
cannot_be_seen: INR checks done at another clinic or by a home meter and not recorded here, and whether the next check is already booked.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm today the date and value of the latest INR, including any clinic or home result, and review whether prompt testing is needed?
